title: Finite clopen rectangular extension from a closed subspace of a profinite power
statement: Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $T$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological space, let $k\geq1$ be an integer, and give $T^k$ the finite product topology. Let $K\subseteq T^k$ be closed with its subspace topology, let $M$ be a finite abelian group with the discrete topology, and let $c:K\to M$ be continuous. A finite clopen partition means a finite collection of pairwise disjoint nonempty subsets, each open and closed, whose union is the whole space; the partition of the empty space is empty. There exist such a partition $\alpha$ of $T$ and a continuous $h:T^k\to M$ such that $h|_K=c$ and $h$ is constant on every product cell $A_0\times\cdots\times A_{k-1}$ with $A_i\in\alpha$. On each cell disjoint from $K$, $h$ is identically $0$. Empty $T$ or $K$ and the zero group are allowed.

source.place: Tags 08ZY (lemma-profinite) and 08ZZ (lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering), finite clopen partitions. Agent-formulated auxiliary assertion, not a standalone assertion of these tags; the rectangular-neighbourhood and atom-refinement argument of the returned proof of lem-sfb-finite-valued-cech-cocycle-descent, steps 2 and 3.

proof.text: If $T=\varnothing$, then $T^k=K=\varnothing$ since $k\geq1$; take the empty partition and unique $h$. If $T\ne\varnothing$ but $K=\varnothing$, take $\alpha=\{T\}$ and $h=0$. Henceforth assume $K\ne\varnothing$.

source.place: Tags 08ZY (lemma-profinite) and 08ZZ (lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering); agent-written rectangular refinement argument using the clopen basis and finite Boolean atoms.

proof.text: For each $x\in K$, continuity into discrete $M$ makes $c^{-1}(\{c(x)\})$ open in $K$. By the subspace topology choose ambient open $O_x\subseteq T^k$ with $K\cap O_x=c^{-1}(\{c(x)\})$. The finite product topology gives opens $U_{x,i}$ with $x\in\prod_{i<k}U_{x,i}\subseteq O_x$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-clopen-basis] in each coordinate to obtain clopen $V_{x,i}$ with $x_i\in V_{x,i}\subseteq U_{x,i}$. Thus $R_x=\prod_{i<k}V_{x,i}$ is open, contains $x$, and $c=c(x)$ on $K\cap R_x$.

source.place: Tags 08ZY (lemma-profinite) and 08ZZ (lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering); agent-written rectangular refinement argument using the clopen basis and finite Boolean atoms.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-tychonoff-product-quasi-compact], $T^k$ is compact. The opens $R_x$ for $x\in K$, together with $T^k\setminus K$, cover $T^k$ because $K$ is closed. Take a finite subcover and discard the complement of $K$: this leaves $R_{x_1},\ldots,R_{x_N}$ covering $K$, since a point of $K$ never belonged to that complement. Thus $N\geq1$ and each selected rectangle retains the value $c(x_j)$ on $K\cap R_{x_j}$.

source.place: Tag 08ZU (theorem-tychonov), followed by the open-cover definition of compactness and the closedness hypothesis on K.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal F=\{V_{x_j,i}:1\leq j\leq N,\ i<k\}$. For every $\epsilon:\mathcal F\to\{0,1\}$ form $A_\epsilon=\bigcap_{V\in\mathcal F}W_{V,\epsilon(V)}$, where $W_{V,1}=V$ and $W_{V,0}=T\setminus V$. There are at most $2^{|\mathcal F|}$ atoms; discard the empty ones. Using all coordinates in the same $\mathcal F$ gives one finite clopen partition $\alpha$ of $T$: every point has its unique membership pattern, different patterns give disjoint sets, and finite intersections of clopens are clopen.

source.place: Tags 08ZY (lemma-profinite) and 08ZZ (lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering); agent-written rectangular refinement argument using the clopen basis and finite Boolean atoms.

proof.text: For any cell $C=\prod_{i<k}A_i$ with $A_i\in\alpha$ meeting $K$, choose $y\in C\cap K$ and a selected rectangle $R_{x_j}$ containing $y$. Since $A_i$ has constant membership in $V_{x_j,i}$ and contains $y_i\in V_{x_j,i}$, we have $A_i\subseteq V_{x_j,i}$ for every $i$. Hence $C\subseteq R_{x_j}$, so $c$ is constant on $C\cap K$. If another selected rectangle meets $C\cap K$, both of its assigned values equal $c(y)$ at a point of $C\cap K$; thus the value on that cell is unique.

source.place: Tags 08ZY (lemma-profinite) and 08ZZ (lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering); agent-written rectangular refinement argument using the clopen basis and finite Boolean atoms.

proof.text: The cells partition $T^k$, since each coordinate belongs to a unique $\alpha$-block. Assign to a cell meeting $K$ the unique value of $c$ on its intersection with $K$, and assign $0\in M$ to every other cell. Define $h(t)$ to be the assigned value of the cell containing $t$. Then $h|_K=c$, $h$ is constant on each cell, and it is zero on every cell disjoint from $K$.

source.place: Tags 08ZY (lemma-profinite) and 08ZZ (lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering); agent-written rectangular refinement argument using the clopen basis and finite Boolean atoms.

proof.text: Every cell is open, being a finite intersection of coordinate inverse images of open blocks. For any open $B\subseteq M$, $h^{-1}(B)$ is the union of cells whose assigned values lie in $B$, hence open. Thus $h$ is continuous. If $M=0$, every assigned value is $0$, so the same construction also covers the zero group.

lean.statement: theorem profinite_rectangular_extension (T : Type u) [TopologicalSpace T] [CompactSpace T] [T2Space T] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace T] (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (K : Set (Fin k → T)) (hK : IsClosed K) (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Finite M] [TopologicalSpace M] [DiscreteTopology M] (c : C(K, M)) : ∃ (α : DiscreteQuotient T) (h : C((Fin k → T), M)), (∀ x : K, h x.val = c x) ∧ (∀ x y : Fin k → T, (∀ i : Fin k, α.proj (x i) = α.proj (y i)) → h x = h y) ∧ (∀ a : Fin k → α, Disjoint {x : Fin k → T | ∀ i : Fin k, α.proj (x i) = a i} K → ∀ x : Fin k → T, (∀ i : Fin k, α.proj (x i) = a i) → h x = 0)
